thread:
Alex: paging oncall — incident-bot just created P0 for increased tail latency on hosted/text-gen in us-west :rotating_light:  customers seeing 500s and timeouts. I’m primary right now but I need to hand off in ~35m. Can someone take primary for the next 2h? runbook link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/latency-tail.md
IncidentBot: Incident P0 created by alex — impacted service: hosted/text-gen — detected 2026-03-15T02:15:00Z — Alert: 95th latency > 1.2s for 15m — Paging oncall. See /incidents/P0-2765432100 for details.
Maria: I can take primary now, switching over. I’ll look at infra (GPUs, autoscaler, AZ imbalance).
Sam: I’ll run runtime checks — model fallback and KV cache health. tagging @maria for autoscaler logs.
Alex: thanks. handoff note: primary should own customer comms until Lucy posts an update. secondary keeps monitoring and triages.
Lucy: I’m here — support will prepare a short status for impacted customers, ETA on a first update ~10m. any concrete error messages we should include?
Maria: infra findings so far: a subset of instances in us-west-2a showing high GPU memory pressure + OOMs. Node drain events around 02:10. Checking autoscaler events.
Sam: runtime quick check: KV cache hit-rate dropped to 12% on that cluster in the last 20m. That explains token regen and latency. Also seeing model fallback to a larger variant for some requests. Will post logs.
Jess: Security quick check: any PII or credential leakage in logs? If it's just OOMs/latency not likely, but I’ll watch logs and access patterns while you triage.
Maria: autoscaler log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T02:09:58Z autoscaler: scale-down candidate pod terminated (node-preempt) reason=spot_interrupt
2026-03-15T02:10:03Z cluster-autoscaler: scale-up requested count=3
2026-03-15T02:11:30Z node-provisioner: provisioning delayed (quota) region=us-west-2a
```

Maria: seems like spot interruptions + quota throttling. provisioning delayed caused capacity hole.
Sam: runtime command I ran: `rtictl cache inspect --cluster=us-west-2a --stat=kv_hit_rate` -> 12%. Also `rtictl model-status --cluster=us-west-2a` shows fallback to model-xx-large under load.
Alex: good context. Maria, can you surface if we can temporarily route traffic to us-west-2b/c while nodes come up? We need to avoid broad customer impact.
Maria: we can failover some routes. Rolling route change via routing console: set route priority for hosted/text-gen to prefer 2b/c. That should be safe but will increase latency for some customers. Anyone object?
Sam: runtime note: routing change will cause cold starts for some shards; expect a transient spike in requests hitting model-loading code. But overall safer than sustained OOMs. I'll prepare cache warming snippets.
Lucy: customer update draft: "We’re investigating increased latency/timeouts for text generation in us-west. Our on-call team has identified capacity issues and is actively mitigating by rebalancing traffic. We’ll update in 15 minutes or sooner. — Redwood Support" any edits?
Jess: add "no evidence of data exposure at this time" if true.
Alex: good call. Lucy add that. Also include guidance: "If you are running critical jobs, pause and retry later"
Lucy: updated and posting to status page and affected customers group.
Maria: initiating routing change now. command: `routingctl set-priority --service=hosted/text-gen --from=us-west-2a --to=us-west-2b,us-west-2c --weight=0.7,0.3`
Sam: starting cache-warm procedure: will prefetch common prefixes and keep model-worker pool warm. snippet: 

```
# warm 10 workers in us-west-2b
rtictl warm-workers --cluster=us-west-2b --count=10 --prompt="Hello"
```

Maria: autoscaler has asked for quota increase, but that may take time. provisioning in progress for 2 instances (ETA ~8m).
Alex: re: handoff — Maria, since you’re primary, can you confirm ownership in ~30m so I can log off? If you need a formal secondary, call it out.
Maria: I’ll stay primary for the next 90m. Sam you’ll be secondary?
Sam: copying. I’ll be secondary and watch model fallbacks / cache metrics. I’ll also coordinate with runtime infra if more nodes needed.
Jess: I’ll keep looking at access logs and will flag any anomalous data movements.
Lucy: I posted the customer update and pinged the top 10 impacted accounts. Support channel for handoffs: #support-critical-incidents.
Alex: quick checklist for handoff note (put in incident doc): 1) current mitigation steps (routing change, warming) 2) expected ETA for capacity (8-12m) 3) who to page next (Maria primary, Sam secondary, Jess security, Lucy support) 4) runbook pointer: https://redwood.example/runbooks/latency-tail.md#failover
Maria: noting coverage gap: nights next 2 days we have only one infra engineer on call 00:00-08:00 UTC — might be rough if spot interruptions keep happening. I’ll leave an action to request extra coverage from oncall-schedule.
Sam: if more capacity gap, propose temporary routing policy to divert non-PLG traffic to cheaper fallbacks to reduce pressure on hosted API. Need product approval though.
Alex: logged that as action item in incident doc. Also flagging for ops leads for schedule fill.
IncidentBot: Incident P0-2765432100 status updated: mitigation in progress — routing change applied — monitoring for 15m. Next update scheduled in 10m.
Maria: monitoring: 95th latency dropping from 1.4s -> 0.9s after routing change, error rate down 60%. provisioning still coming up.
Sam: cache hit-rate recovering to 42% in 6m after warmers. model fallback events reduced.
Lucy: second customer update posted: "Mitigation applied — we’re rebalancing traffic and warming capacity. Error rates and latency improving. We’ll keep monitoring and will post when fully restored."
Jess: no security anomalies so far. thumbs up.
Alex: thanks team. Maria keep primary. Sam stay ready. I’ll sign out in 25m and will add a short handoff entry to the incident doc before I go.
Maria: will do. If things degrade again, page runtime and infra together using `#oncall` — we might need an emergency double-page.
Sam: noted. I’ll add a monitoring alert tweak to reduce false positives from cold-start spikes.
Lucy: support ready to escalate to account teams if any VIPs report.
Alex: last note before I go: add any runbook deviations to the incident doc under "deviations" so we can review in postmortem.
Maria: copied. marking timeline events in /incidents/P0-2765432100/timeline.
